history.caveat: Announcement DATES are estimated by applying this quarter's notified lag backwards to prior period ends; the move is the largest within +/-2 trading days of that estimate. This is a cadence prior, not a record that a print happened on that date. Use it as a scale for how much this name moves, never as evidence about a particular past date.

positioning.basis: absent from the JPX register, so no disclosed position at or above the 0.5% threshold. A real zero, not missing data -- but the threshold truncates, so 0.4% and 0.0% are both recorded here as 0.0.

expected_move.basis: the larger of (a) the median of twelve ESTIMATED prior reactions and (b) a one-session move implied by 20-day realised volatility. It is NOT an option-implied move: nothing is paying for it, and it carries no information about what the market expects from THIS print. It is a scale for how far this name travels.

baseline.priced_lean_basis: Sum of the components above. Read researcher_japan/scripts/jp_priced_in.py, lean_components(): every weight is a PRIOR, none is measured on Japanese data, and jp_resolve.py ranks each component separately so measurement can replace them. evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is the domestic same-store-sales line and this name has NOT paid for it. evidence.text: AZO's LIFO reserve has been built entirely by tariff inflation - the 10-Q states 'Due to price changes on the Company's merchandise purchases, primarily due to inflation driven by tariffs, the Company's LIFO credit reserve balance was $260.0 million at May 9, 2026, and $83.0 million at August 30, 2025' - and Q4 FY26 carries the easiest LIFO comp of the year (guided ~$30m charge, 45bp, against an actual $80m charge / 128bp in Q4 FY25), with upside to a credit if supplier pass-back of IEEPA refunds lowers replacement cost in the May-August window, which is the exact line the stock has been sold on for three consecutive quarters.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Gross margin with LIFO as the swing factor is the stated cause of the last three selloffs: Q3 FY26 gross margin 52.2%, -57bp, with a 77bp LIFO charge cited as the primary driver, and the stock fell 8.99%; Q4 FY25 gross margin 51.5%, -98bp on a 128bp LIFO impact, and EPS fell 5.6% reported against +8.7% ex-LIFO. The market has punished this line hard when it went the wrong way; it has never been tested with it going the right way on this name, which is why the band is wide and the point estimate is small.
evidence.why_not_priced: Only the delta to the guide is unpriced and I say so: the $30m Q4 charge was guided on the 2026-05-26 call, so the +83bp YoY improvement is inside what the company already told the market to expect and is a reported-quarter item. What is not in any preview I could find is that the reserve is now $260m built from tariff inflation that the Supreme Court voided on 2026-02-20, and that peer retailers are already booking the reversal - AAP took $26m of tariff refunds worth 130bp of gross margin in its July quarter, Target applied $685m of $730m of refunds to reduce COGS, and ORLY says it is negotiating supplier sharing of refunds. If the market had priced a possible LIFO credit rather than the guided charge, the sell-side gross-margin cuts into this print would not be running the other way.
evidence.independence: Independent of finding 1 - different document (the 10-Q, not a peer transcript) and a different P&L line (gross margin, not comp). Corroboration from a different source: https://www.supplychaindive.com/news/oreilly-automotive-suppliers-sharing-tariff-refund-benefits/827111/ on supplier pass-back, and AAP's own $26m / 130bp refund benefit in the quarter ending mid-July. The counterweight I have already netted into the 0.6: the upside-to-guide leg rests on other retailers' cost behaviour, not on an AZO document, and AZO itself reports and is modelled on ex-LIFO EPS, so the market has a habit of looking through this line in both directions.

evidence.text: The FY2026 10-K, due roughly late October 2026, is where the full-year LIFO reserve roll-forward and any IEEPA tariff refund or gain-contingency disclosure will appear in primary form; CBP's CAPE liquidation process was still running at ~$128.7bn of accepted refunds as of 2026-07-31, so supplier pass-back to AZO continues to accrue after this print.

evidence.text: German new-registration data published by the Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt shows Wohnmobile down 15.7% in July 2026 and down 21.4% in August 2026 - a two-month collapse in Erwin Hymer's home market against a January-July cumulative of only -3.3% - while Thor's European segment was still shipping +4.2% units and +11.8% net sales in the February-April quarter with backlog up just 1.0%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Europe is where this stock's last two large negative reactions originated: 2025-12-03 -9.48% and 2026-03-03 -5.56%, both quarters in which the FY26 EPS guide was under pressure. But the line has also gone the other way: on 2026-06-03 Thor cut the FY26 EPS guide from $3.75-4.25 to $3.30-3.80 and the stock rose 2.86%, and on 2025-09-24 it set an initial FY26 guide implying a 13-23% EPS decline and rose 6.10%. This is why the size is -2.0 and not larger.
evidence.why_not_priced: The number is a single line item ('-21,4 %/1,9 %') inside a German-language KBA passenger-car press release published on 2026-09-03, eighteen days before this print. Every English-language THO preview I found anchors on RVIA wholesale and SSI retail, which are North American series; BMO's pre-print estimate cut was explicitly on 'softer retail and shipment trends' in the RV sector, i.e. the US data. The publicly circulating European datapoint is CIVD's seven-month figure of -3.0% overall and -3.3% for motor caravans, which is an order of magnitude milder than what July and August actually did, and CIVD's own Caravan Salon messaging in early September was that the industry 'expects recovery once the economic situation improves'. If the market had this, Thor's European segment - the leg that has grown net sales double digits for three straight quarters and carries ~38% of revenue - would be the thing preview notes name, and it is not. Net of the rest of the company [sizing note removed]: North America is ~62% of revenue and my read there is mildly positive, Thor Europe is taking share (24.4%, up), European backlog is +1.0% rather than falling, and the euro is roughly 3-4% stronger year on year (https://www.federalreserve.gov/releases/h10/hist/dat00_eu.htm), so the reported European quarter can still be up in dollars. That is why this is filed as a guidance finding about FY27 European wholesale and not as a reported-quarter finding, and why it is sized -2.0 rather than the -4.5 the retail number alone would suggest. Caveat I am carrying explicitly: KBA's 'Wohnmobile' is a Pkw sub-category and is narrower than CIVD's 'Reisemobile', so the two series are not identical in definition.
evidence.independence: Knaus Tabbert, the listed German motorhome maker and Erwin Hymer's closest domestic competitor, reported H1 2026 revenue of EUR 503.9m, -11.9%, units -8.0%, and narrowed its FY26 adjusted EBITDA margin band to 5.0-6.0% citing 'weakened end-customer demand since spring' and 'continued cautious ordering behaviour from dealers' (https://www.boerse-online.de/dpa-afx/eqs-news-knaus-tabbert-veroeffentlicht-halbjahresfinanzbericht-2026-deutsch-543273.html, snippet_only - I read this from search output, not a successful fetch). Separately, a wave of German motorhome dealer and rental insolvencies through 2026 - Vanever/FreeVenture (7 August 2026), Schafhaeutle Reisemobile, HECK Caravan, amo caravaning, CMS Reisemobile - is documented at https://ms-aktuell.de/welt/vanever-insolvenz-wohnmobile-21-08-2026/ (2026-08-21, date confirmed in the URL path and in the body). These are different documents from the KBA release and point the same way.

What stops me sizing this larger, and I am resolving rather than leaving the contradiction to be added by the sum [sizing note removed]: a bottom-up cross-check from RVIA monthly shipments over May-July 2026 (industry -14.7%, towables ~-15.3%, motorhomes ~-10.4%) applied to Q4 FY25 segment revenue of $888.7m / $557.4m / $923.1m lands at roughly $2.15bn, essentially at consensus, while backlog-conversion off the 30 April 2026 segment backlogs (-39.1% / -13.3% / +1.0%) lands at roughly $1.96bn, essentially at the guide midpoint. The two methods bracket $1.96-2.15bn, so my honest point estimate is about $2.09bn, ~3.5% below the bar - a real but small miss, and a miss that lands inside a range the company already guided to, which [sizing note removed].

evidence.text: On 2026-09-10, twelve days before this print, Thor abandoned the decentralised operating model it has run for decades and put all North American RV operations under a single president and a single CFO, with the stated objective of 'drive out costs within the Company to strengthen our earnings profile' and benefits on an 'accelerated timeline' relative to the two-group structure announced earlier.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name has paid for a self-help framing at a Q4 print before: on 2025-09-24, the equivalent event a year ago, Thor set an FY26 guide implying a 13-23% EPS decline off FY25's $4.85 and the stock rose 6.10%. The 2026-06-03 print, where management first put margin and cost language around a cut guide, went +2.86%. Both of the events on this line that carried a cost/structure narrative were bought.
evidence.why_not_priced: The release was filed as a leadership-change announcement and the market read it as personnel: the stock is -5.38% over the five sessions to the seal and made a new leg toward its 52-week low after it. What the document actually contains is a structural reorganisation of a famously decentralised manufacturer with an explicit margin objective and no number attached, arriving twelve days before the one print of the year at which this company sets full-year guidance. If the market had priced it you would expect the pre-print drift to be positive rather than -5.38%, and you would expect at least one of the three pre-print analyst actions I could find (BofA target $96 to $86 on 2026-09-21, BMO estimate cuts, Wall Street Zen to Sell on 2026-09-20) to frame FY27 around a cost programme rather than around 'softer retail and shipment trends'. The inference I am making - that the FY27 guide arrives with a quantified structural-savings element - is an inference and not a disclosed number, which is why this is +1.5 and not larger.
evidence.independence: The earlier two-group reorganisation is a separate release at https://ir.thorindustries.com/investor-resources/press-releases/press-release-details/2026/THOR-INDUSTRIES-ANNOUNCES-STRATEGIC-EVOLUTION-OF-NORTH-AMERICAN-OPERATING-MODEL-WITH-FORMATION-OF-TWO-RV-GROUPS/default.aspx (date not independently confirmed by me; the 2026-09-10 release references it as 'previously announced'). Corroborating, the Indiana Department of Workforce Development's current WARN list carries no 2026 notice from any Thor entity (https://www.in.gov/dwd/warn-notices/current-warn-notices/, read 2026-09-21) despite a 25% decline in towable unit shipments - Thor has been taking cost out through structure rather than through plant closures, which is consistent with the operating-model route and inconsistent with a capacity-cut route.

evidence.text: Camping World, Thor's largest customer and holder of record US new-unit share above 29%, exited its June 2026 quarter with new vehicles on the lot down ~17% year on year in units (dollars down only ~5%), prior-model-year exposure on new RVs near 1% against over 6% a year earlier, and units aged more than 365 days cut by over 60%.

A dealer-restock framing at a Q4 print has been bought on this name.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced, and I am sizing it accordingly at +1.0. This is a direct counterparty speaking after Thor last guided [sizing note removed], and it is the single largest offset to the 'channel is still stuffed' read that the RVIA-minus-SSI gap generates - US retail registrations ran -19.0% in May and -20.7% in June against wholesale of -18.7% and -13.1%, which looks like inventory building until you find that the largest single buyer's lot is 17% lighter in units with almost no carryover model years. The reason it is not fully in the price is that it is eight weeks old, sits in a competitor's transcript rather than in any THO preview, and cuts against the direction every RV headline since has taken. If the market had folded it in, the pre-print commentary would be about a 2027 restock rather than about 'softer retail and shipment trends'. evidence.independence: The quarter itself is in the primary 8-K exhibit at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001669779/000110465926088141/cwh-20260729xex99d1.htm (2026-07-29), a different document from the transcript. Management stated exactly this on the 2026-07-15 call — 'The first quarter of fiscal year 27 has 1 extra day... The second quarter has the same number of workdays. Applying management's own stated elasticity — fuel is ~100bp of revenue and a 20% fuel price move is ~20bp of margin — the YoY fuel headwind eases by roughly 2bp quarter-on-quarter, i.e. nothing. Dropped rather than filed.

evidence.text: CarMax's own ABS servicer reports through August 2026 show no new credit deterioration in the securitised Tier 1 book, which the 10-Q puts at 95.6% of the portfolio. The 2025-3 trust at 13 months (31+ day delinquency 1.75%, cumulative net loss 0.49%) tracks 2024-3 at the same age a year earlier (1.63%, 0.60%). The problem 2023 vintage (trust 2023-4) deteriorated April to August 2026 by +1.22pp of delinquency, against +1.11pp over the same months of 2025, and its cumulative net loss accrual slowed. So a repeat of Q2 FY26's $71.3m reserve build for the 2022-2023 vintages looks unlikely.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Credit has been the downside line. Q2 FY26 (2025-09-25) fell 20.07% on a $142.2m provision that included the $71.3m vintage build (https://investors.carmax.com/news-and-events/news/news-details/2025/CarMax-Reports-Second-Quarter-Fiscal-Year-2026-Results/default.aspx). Q1 FY27 (2026-06-17) fell 8.98% partly on CAF credit worry about Tier 2 expansion, even though the provision fell to $95.6m. The market punishes credit surprises. The absence of one has not been shown to pay.
evidence.why_not_priced: Previews cite only the May allowance ratio (2.95%, up from 2.78%) and the Manheim index as the credit tells (traderc 2026-09-19). None cites the June-August trust data. If the market had read these reports, put skew would not still be rising into the print on a name whose last big credit shock was a vintage build. ORTEX has put/call 2.4 standard deviations above its average. The caveat, which the size reflects: consensus EPS up 11.5% YoY already assumes no repeat build, so this removes a tail rather than moving the bar. The Tier 2 book, whose day-one provisions are the live worry, is not in these trusts.
evidence.independence: Same document family, different trusts and dates: 2024-3 August 2025 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2029255/000202925525000048/a2024-3ex991091525.htm); 2023-4 August 2026 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1995430/000199543026000047/a2023-4ex991091526.htm), April 2026 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1995430/000199543026000025/a2023-4ex991051526.htm), August 2025 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1995430/000199543025000048/a2023-4ex991091525.htm) and April 2025 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1995430/000199543025000025/a2023-4ex991051525.htm); 2024-4 August 2026, 22 months old, 2.04% delinquency and 0.86% cumulative net loss (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2037519/000203751926000048/a2024-4ex991091526.htm).
